title: Bitcoin Slides to About $67,000, Below Its 200-Week Average; MSCI Exit Weighs on Strategy
dek: Bitcoin traded near $67,200 early Saturday, below its 200-week moving average, as spot ETF outflows continued and Strategy faces its MSCI index exit at the end of November.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Black-and-white photograph of an automatic ticker apparatus on the New York Stock Exchange trading floor
image.credit: Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: Saturday update: Bitcoin was at $67,204.86 at 4:13 a.m. ET on Nov. 14 (CoinDesk price page), below its 200-week moving average and down more than 10% for the week (CoinSpectator).
Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Friday for the first time since August and traded near $68,600 at 11:59 a.m. ET, down more than 4% over 24 hours (Investopedia; Yahoo Finance).
Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $299.8 million on Wednesday, their fifth straight day of net outflows, for about $1.44 billion over those five days (Bitcoin Magazine).
MSCI will remove Strategy from its USA Index at the Nov. 30 close, which also takes it out of the MSCI World and ACWI indexes (CoinReporter; Yahoo Finance).
Strategy shares fell as much as 6% on Thursday (Yahoo Finance live report) and about 7% at the open (Bitcoin Magazine).
body:
Bitcoin fell below $72,000 on Thursday, Nov. 12, its lowest level since mid-August, as traders absorbed a hotter inflation report, higher bets on a December Federal Reserve rate hike and a sharp drop in Strategy, the largest corporate holder of the token.

## Saturday update

Bitcoin traded near $67,200 early Saturday, below its 200-week moving average. CoinSpectator put the loss so far this week at more than 10%, with selling continuing below $70,000 (CoinSpectator, Nov. 14); estimates of the weekly decline vary by data provider and cutoff time. Decrypt's data showed spot bitcoin ETFs shed $185.4 million on Nov. 13, a seventh straight day of outflows. We could not verify a 24-hour liquidation total from CoinDesk, The Block or CoinGlass in this run, so no liquidation figure is given.

## The price move

Bitcoin Magazine reported that the token was near $71,800 at the time of writing on Thursday morning. Yahoo Finance's live coverage said bitcoin was down about 8% so far in November. Bitcoin.com reported that crypto derivatives liquidations topped $650 million over 24 hours, with long positions unwinding as prices slipped.

The slide follows a week in which bitcoin tracked the tech sector. It fell on Monday when the Nvidia probe weighed on markets, then lagged Wednesday's rebound in chip stocks, according to Bitcoin Magazine.

## The index exit

MSCI confirmed on Wednesday evening that Strategy will leave its USA Index as part of its November 2026 review. The removal also takes the company out of the MSCI World and ACWI indexes, effective at the Nov. 30 close. Metaplanet, the Japanese bitcoin treasury company, is slated for removal from MSCI's Japan Small Cap index on the same date (CoinReporter).

Index funds will sell Strategy shares, not bitcoin. Nothing in the index rules requires Strategy to sell its own coins. The effect is more indirect: a weaker share price makes it harder for the company to raise capital for new purchases. Strategy's CEO Phong Le pointed to $21 billion raised so far this year on the company's October earnings call, according to Yahoo Finance.

## Flows and rates

Spot bitcoin ETFs continued to see withdrawals. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $269.7 million of Wednesday's redemptions, its ninth straight session of outflows, Bitcoin Magazine reported.

Rates matter here too. Thursday's jobless claims report did not ease the outlook for Fed policy, and CME FedWatch still shows traders pricing a quarter-point December hike. Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, which has kept pressure on bitcoin all week, Bitcoin Magazine said.

## What to watch

The October producer price index was released at 8:30 a.m. ET Friday, at +0.3% against a 0.4% forecast (BLS; CNBC). Investors will also watch whether bitcoin holds the $70,000 area that analysts cited as the next support level, and whether the MSCI effective date on Nov. 30 brings forced selling in Strategy shares.

This is market analysis. The figures above come from the cited outlets and are not a forecast of future prices.

## Late-session print

By 3:59 p.m. ET, MarketAlleys showed bitcoin at $71,415, down 4.32% over 24 hours. That is one secondary aggregator; other Thursday quotes ran from about $72,700 to $73,500 earlier in the session (Yahoo Finance; Substack). The MSCI removal of Strategy takes effect after the close on Nov. 30 (Yahoo Finance).

## Friday update

Bitcoin fell below $70,000 early Friday, Nov. 13, for the first time since August, and traded near $68,600 at 11:59 a.m. ET, down more than 4% over 24 hours (Investopedia, citing CoinDesk). Strategy shares were down nearly 5% at the same time (Investopedia).

marketImpact.summary: The crypto selloff is coming from three directions: a weak spot-ETF tape, a hawkish rates backdrop and a forced-selling overhang on Strategy from the MSCI exit. The index effect is mechanical and dated, so the Nov. 30 close is the clearest catalyst.
